newsitem.title: CHILE: Enaex wins $90 mln loan for plant.
newsitem.headline: Enaex wins $90 mln loan for plant.

text.p: Chilean chemical and explosives maker Enaex SA, controlled by Grupo Sigdo Koppers, signed a $90 million loan with a syndicate of banks led by Chase Manhattan, the bank said.

Enaex, a big chemical supplier to the copper industry and Latin America's largest explosives maker, will use the money to build a $350 million plant making explosives-grade ammonia nitrate in Mejillones, said a statement.
The seven-year loan includes a two-year grace period. Chase Manhattan and Enaex signed the loan for the new plant Thursday morning in Santiago.
By locating the new plant in Mejillones, 60 km north of Antofagasta, Enaex will be able to supply the whole domestic market for the chemical and also export to Peru, Bolivia and Argentina, it said.
Chilean engineering firm Sigdo Koppers controls 50 percent of Enaex and 20 percent is owned by U.S. explosives maker Austin Powder Co.
